cases.title: negative zero survives the conversion of a value held in memory (O1)
cases.note: an evaluator-level case: no flow input can carry -0, which jsonb stores as 0

cases.title: a __proto__ key sets the prototype, not an own property
cases.note: built with JSON.parse, the value would give [["__proto__"],null,true]

cases.title: a results read of the previous step served from memory is the rebuilt previous_result
cases.note: a returned JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{"x":1}}'), an object with an own __proto__ key; b directly after a reads it from memory (JE-18 rule 1), the previous_result global itself, so the key set the prototype

cases.title: a fetched results read is built by JSON.parse, so a __proto__ key is an own property
cases.note: a step m between a and b: the read fetches a's stored result and parses it with JSON.parse, so nothing is inherited

cases.title: the previous step's results read is the previous_result object itself
cases.note: rule 1 of JE-18 returns the previous_result global, not a copy

cases.title: a read that fetches at the read uses JSON.parse as it is then
cases.note: JSON.parse is looked up when the fetched text is parsed, so a replacement made before a computed read of a step that no static read names gives the read its return value (JE-16, JE-12 consequence 4); the helpers resource and flow_user_state read the same way

cases.title: a static read was parsed by the prefetch, before the expression could replace JSON.parse
cases.note: the prefetch resolves every step the text names before the expression's code runs (JE-12), so its parse is the engine's own

cases.title: a __proto__ of null clears the prototype, and one of any other value is dropped
a __proto__ key written with escapes is the same key
